newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt in limbo in London before FOMC meet.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt in limbo in London before FOMC meet.

text.p: Emerging market debt drifted gently into the London trading day with players mostly sidelined ahead of today's FOMC meeting.
Eastern European debt showed a little life, with Bulgarian paper gapping up from earlier lows and Russian paper easing a touch in the absence of any fresh news on Yeltsin's health.
But traders stressed volumes were thin and activity light.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR climbed 1/2 a point to 44-1/4 but on virtually no volume. Russian dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR softened slightly to 65-1/8 after opening in London at 65-1/2.

"In Bulgaria there's been demand from some dedicated funds, but it's more a combination of new money after its rate hike, which makes the government look more serious, and a technical short squeeze," said one dealer at a US house here.

On Monday Bulgaria raised its main interest rate to 300 percent from 108 percent, boosting prices of Bulgarian debt which had missed out on last week's market rally due to concerns over the slow pace of its IMF reforms.
Otherwise prices from Latin America to eastern Europe were mainly flat as the market awaited the results of the FOMC meeting, which could spark a 25 basis point rise in official interest rates.
With the market split on the likely outcome of the meeting, emerging debt hung in limbo through the morning.
Traders said a quarter point rate rise would spark a fall of around 5/8 in debt prices in Mexico -- the market which, with Argentina, is most sensitive to the U.S. interest rate regime.
"You would see about 5/8 of a point downside in most of these assets depending on the fall in Treasuries," said one dealer.

"In the first drop spreads will hold in well in the Latins, if there is a 25 b.p. rise, but if there is no change in rates spreads won't tighten as much -- those who have gone long may want to shed paper," he added.
Mexico's UMS-26 MXUMS=RR was bid at 95-5/8 at 1050 GMT, Brazilian C's were 1/8 softer at 68-7/8, and Argentine FRBs were flat at 82-3/4. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
